extraction_warnings: Study is a metagenomic catalog/discovery study across 9,428 samples from 46 datasets spanning multiple countries, body sites, and age groups. Individual sample-level metadata (subject_id, sample_id, per-sample age, per-sample body_site) are not disclosed in the paper; they are only available through NCBI-SRA or supplementary tables.
No case-control designation: this is a descriptive microbiome catalog study, not a case-control study.
Age groups are reported as aggregate counts but individual sample ages are not provided in the text.
Madagascar and Ethiopia cohorts are the only newly sequenced populations; other 9,316 samples are from public repositories with heterogeneous metadata.
The paper emphasizes lifestyle (Westernized vs non-Westernized) as a key variable but does not provide formal lifestyle classifications for individual samples within the text.
Antibiotic exposure history and other clinical covariates are not reported in this paper.
The study does not involve periodontal measurements despite including oral cavity samples.

This paper is a microbiome genomics study focused on reconstructing and cataloging microbial genomes from human metagenomes. Most fields in the provided schema relate to human clinical, demographic, and medical phenotype data. The paper does not report individual-level participant phenotypes such as age, BMI, disease status, treatment, etc. at the granularity required by the schema. Instead, it reports aggregated metadata across 9,428 metagenomes from 46 datasets spanning multiple countries, body sites, and age categories.

The Madagascar and Ethiopian cohorts are briefly described with minimal phenotypic data: Madagascar cohort includes 112 healthy volunteers (54F, 58M) from non-Westernized communities; Ethiopian cohort includes 5 female individuals. No detailed participant-level phenotypes are provided.
Only study-level granularity is appropriate here. The paper does not report individual sample metadata at the level of detail that the schema expects.

This paper is a microbiome genomics study, not a clinical trial or disease study. Most clinical/biomarker fields in the schema (biomarker_name/value/unit, disease_response_os, ECOG status, tumor measurements) do not apply and are correctly marked as not_reported.
The feces_phenotype_value field contains metagenomic mappability metrics and microbiome diversity percentages rather than traditional phenotypic measurements.
The paper reports aggregate study-level statistics and does not provide individual sample-level data in a structured tabular format suitable for sample-level extraction.
No participant-level clinical outcomes or disease progression data are reported in this microbiome resource paper.
